title: Carry a picked tote by its end hand holds and seat it on the tote on a pick cart
instruction: Stack the tote in the left bay onto the tote in the right bay, seated and square, and let go.
context: Stockers and order fillers (SOC 53-7065, about 2.8 million US jobs) and hand laborers and material movers (SOC 53-7062, about 3.0 million), BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, build pick-cart stacks by lifting a picked tote and setting it on another many times a shift. A loaded tote is lifted by the two end hand holds (the long sides are smooth), so it takes both hands carrying together. The foot then has to be seated blind: from above the hands and the tote hide the lower tote's rim, and one set down more than about 10 mm off rides on the wall tops, so the stack slides or topples at the first corner. Stacking a tote is a common job, but this task tests the rest: a two-handed carry of a loaded tote by its end holds, and seating its foot in the lower tote's lead-in by feel and by the hands' position, not by sight. The cart's locator frames hold each tote in its bay until it is lifted out.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +0.305 m and -0.305 m. (1) A fixed pick cart bed, grey steel: a deck 6 mm thick, 410 x 900 mm (x 80 to 490 mm, y -450 to +450 mm); a locator frame round each of two bays, 6 mm wide and 6 mm tall, 4 mm clear of the tote's foot on all four sides (bays centred at x 240 mm, y +230 mm and y -230 mm, so the two totes stand 60 mm apart end to end); two rear uprights, 25 x 25 x 300 mm at x 470 mm, y +440 and -440 mm, joined by a 25 mm square push handle across the top. (2) Two identical loose totes, blue polypropylene stacking containers, 400 x 300 x 74 mm (Euronorm stacking bin; outer size, 0.48 kg empty weight and closed hand grips on the short sides as in the published datasheet of e.g. Transoplast 9227.V00.522; sizes within 2 mm of nominal, measure yours), walls 3 mm, 0.70 kg each with 0.22 kg of picked goods (a 200 x 260 x 30 mm cardboard carton, tan, on the floor). The long side runs along y. Under the rim each end wall (the 300 mm walls, at y +-200 mm of the tote) has a hand hold (opening and foot sizes are not in datasheets: the sizes below are the specification, check your totes against them): a 110 mm wide, 16 mm tall slot with a 10 mm thick, 12 mm tall grip bar above it, 40 to 52 mm up. Underneath, a 386 x 286 mm foot 12 mm deep with a 45 degree lead-in 6 mm deep; above it a ledge whose underside is 9 mm up. The foot fits inside the lower tote's walls with 4 mm clear on each side, and the ledge then rests on the lower walls' top: seated is 65 mm above the lower tote's foot underside. A foot more than 10 mm off centre does not go in and rides on the wall tops, 74 mm above it. (3) The picked tote stands in the left bay (x 240 mm, y +230 mm), the base tote in the right bay (x 240 mm, y -230 mm), both resting on the deck on their feet, rims up. Each hand carries 3.4 N with both on the bars. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of both totes and both grippers. Seated: the picked tote's foot underside is 65 mm above the base tote's (so its rim is 65 mm above the base tote's rim), within 1 mm; its centre within 4 mm of the base tote's in x and in y; its long axis within 2 degrees of it (top view); its tilt under 1 degree. On the base tote: its centre within 60 mm of the base tote's in x and y, 55 to 90 mm above it, its long axis within 20 degrees of the base tote's, tilt under 20 degrees. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from both totes, and over that 1 s neither tote moves more than 5 mm or turns more than 5 degrees (no visible motion on video; the GPU demo met a stricter 1 mm / 0.3 degree check). Score 0 unless hands off; 0 if at any time either tote's foot goes lower than 3 mm above the table (off the deck) or either tote tilts more than 30 degrees (on its side), or if the base tote is ever more than 10 mm from where it stood or turned or tilted more than 5 degrees. Otherwise: 1.0 seated; 0.5 on the base tote, 62 to 77 mm above it, within 20 mm of its centre in x and y, within 4 degrees of its long axis, tilt under 3 degrees, but not seated (riding on the rim); 0.25 on the base tote otherwise; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial per condition: seated, a rule at each of the four corners from the lower tote's rim to the upper tote's rim (65 mm, within 1 mm; seated, the upper ledge sits on the lower rim with no gap); centred, a rule across both end walls (4 mm); square, a protractor or square on the long edges; tilt, a spirit level or the rim gap (1 degree is 7 mm over 400 mm); base tote undisturbed, pencil marks at its corners; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block and 30 fps video over the last 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Published: 400 x 300 x 74 mm, 0.48 kg, closed end grips. Specified here, not published: foot, ledge, lead-in and grip sizes (a real build matches them, with a printed insert if needed). Totes are thin-walled boxes with 3 mm walls; ribs and lugs omitted. Goods are a rigid carton fixed in the tote (0.70 kg in all, est). Friction 0.30 PP on PP, 0.35 on steel (est). Real totes vary by about 1 mm. The cart is fixed; a real one rolls and is braked.
reset_notes: Stand the base tote in the right bay (x 240 mm, y -230 mm) and the picked tote in the left bay (x 240 mm, y +230 mm), each on its foot inside the locator frame, rims up, long sides along y, a carton of goods on each floor. Nothing is consumed.
